Kyle — appreciate the clarity. Putting together a concise proposal. Main points up front:

1) Aggregation vs per-region billing:
   - We support both models operationally. Default for hosted API is per-region billing (tokens billed at the region where execution occurs) because of tax/VAT and data residency reasons.
   - We can offer an aggregated/blended commit for enterprise customers via a single reserved commit ("bucket") that is invoiced centrally and applied as credits across regions. This requires explicit contract language and a monthly reconciliation appendix.

2) Routing & residency:
   - By default we route to the region closest to the request; we can pin routes for specific customers or API keys to a region to satisfy residency.
   - If you want Redwood to opportunistically route to lower-cost regions for token savings, we can do that but it requires: (a) consent in the SOW, and (b) options for data-at-rest controls (KMS keys per region) to meet EU controls.

3) Ballpark pricing (prelim):
   - Example blended commit (3B tokens/month): base hosted list rate ~ $0.000020/token. With committed monthly 3B we can propose a blended effective rate in the range of $0.000013 - $0.000016/token depending on mix and whether we allow cross-region routing and revenue recognition preferences.
   - If EU tokens are invoiced with VAT and require local entity billing, add a regional surcharge of ~5-8% for EU due to VAT/admin overhead. APAC varies by country; we assume ~3-6% uplift for APAC routing.

I attached a preliminary pricing sheet that models a few scenarios (per-region billing, blended bucket, and opportunistic routing). Also attaching our standard Master Agreement for review.

Next steps I propose:
- I will send a short draft SOW that enumerates routing and data residency options (pinning, opportunistic routing, KMS per-region).
- Stephanie (cc) will run the math for a blended vs per-region invoice and show net monthly invoice impact including VAT assumptions.

Would you like us to show two formal options in the SOW (A = per-region invoices only; B = centralized blended commit w/ reconciliation)?

Best,

Delta & recommendation:
- Blended bucket simplifies procurement and reduces sticker shock on EU invoices but requires Contract Appendix and clear reconciliation cadence.
- For compliance-conscious EU customers, recommend pinning critical EU routes (legal/regulatory traffic) while allowing opportunistic routing for non-sensitive traffic.
